tasks.short: Demonstrate operational procedures on the floor, explain company policies to new staff, prepare training checklists, record who has been trained, and check that workers apply the procedures.

steps.what: Service supervisor trains workers in proper operational procedures by demonstrating them on the floor
Service supervisor explains company policies to new staff
Service supervisor prepares training materials and procedure checklists
Service supervisor records on paper who has been trained in what
Service supervisor checks that workers apply the procedures

tasks.design: Company policies become short modules in the learning system ({LMS}) that new staff read on their phone, so the supervisor answers questions instead of reading out policies. Procedure checklists are kept once in a shared library, and completed modules and checklists show in one training record. Demonstrating on the floor and checking practice stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were explained one by one and training kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems host short modules and record completion.
tasks.still_hard: Reading a policy is not the same as following it on a busy day.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a nervous new worker how to handle a difficult client.

reach.learn: Whether new workers work alone sooner.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can host short policy modules on a phone and record completion.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new worker to procedures checked; hiring is outside.
Input contract: policies from HR; procedures from the supervisor; fallback is explaining in person.
New staff read modules in about the time the supervisor took to explain; no added staff time.
Demonstrating and checking do not change.
research_questions: Do new workers ask fewer policy questions later?

incremental.description: Service supervisor updates modules when policies change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few new workers a year; high: high staff turnover.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend managers' meetings, read e-mails and memos about changes, pass changes to the team at the shift briefing, and note them in the handover book.

steps.what: Service supervisor meets with managers and other supervisors to stay informed of changes affecting operations
Service supervisor reads e-mails and memos about changes
Service supervisor passes changes to the team at the shift briefing
Service supervisor notes the changes in the shift handover book

tasks.design: Managers post operational changes in one announcements channel ({CHAT}) with a start date and the teams affected, instead of scattered e-mails and memos. The shift handover is a shared page that links to those announcements. Meetings with managers and briefing the team stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrived through e-mails, memos and talk on the floor.
tasks.enabler_now: Team chat tools have announcement channels; shared pages hold handover notes.
tasks.still_hard: Managers still send some changes by personal message.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a change so the team accepts it.

reach.learn: Whether one channel cuts missed changes.

evidence.claim: Team chat tools offer announcement channels; shared pages can hold handover notes.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting agenda to the handover note; deciding the changes is outside.
Input contract: changes posted by managers; fallback is e-mail.
Meetings and briefings do not change.
Managers' time to post changes is about the same as writing memos.

incremental.description: Service supervisor reminds managers to post changes in the channel.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few changes a week; high: a fast-changing operation with many memos.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect availability and leave requests, estimate staffing needs from bookings, build the roster, review and adjust it, publish it to staff, and handle shift swaps and sickness.

steps.what: Service supervisor collects staff availability and leave requests from chat messages and paper
Service supervisor estimates staffing needs from bookings and past busy days
Service supervisor assigns work schedules following work requirements in a spreadsheet roster
Service supervisor reviews and adjusts the roster for fairness and service quality
Service supervisor sends the roster to staff
Service supervisor handles shift swaps and sick calls

tasks.design: Staff enter availability and leave in a scheduling app ({HCM}) instead of sending messages. A dashboard forecasts staffing needs from bookings and past busy days. A rule-based scheduler drafts the roster from skills, availability, contract hours and rest times, without ranking staff on behaviour or speed; the supervisor adjusts it, and once approved it is published at least 28 days ahead unless the collective agreement says otherwise. Swaps are requested in the app and checked against the same rules before the supervisor approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters lived in spreadsheets and swaps in chat groups.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling apps collect availability, draft rosters by rules and handle swaps.
tasks.still_hard: Fair rosters need judgement on who did the last bad shifts.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who needs a lighter week after a hard month.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor adjusts and approves rosters instead of building them.

reach.learn: Whether staff swap shifts more easily.

evidence.claim: Shiftbase offers shift scheduling with availability, open shifts, swaps, conflict warnings and auto-scheduling.
Without a collective rule, a roster is announced at least 28 days ahead.
A working-time arrangement and a time clock that can watch attendance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from availability and bookings to roster changes; payroll is outside.
Input contract: availability entered by staff; bookings from the booking system; fallback is chat messages and spreadsheets.
Staff enter availability in the app in about the time they took to send messages; no added staff time.
Reviewing the roster stays with the supervisor.
research_questions: Do last-minute gaps in the roster fall?

incremental.description: Service supervisor keeps skills and contract hours current in the app.

approvals.approved_version: The roster as reviewed and approved by the supervisor in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small team with stable shifts; high: a large team with many part-timers and swaps.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the vacancy, post it on job sites, screen applications, schedule interviews, interview candidates, decide whom to hire, and send the offer.

steps.what: Service supervisor writes the vacancy text
Service supervisor posts the vacancy on job sites one by one
Service supervisor screens applications from e-mail
Service supervisor schedules interviews by phone and e-mail
Service supervisor interviews candidates to recruit staff members
Service supervisor decides whom to hire
Service supervisor e-mails the job offer to the chosen candidate

tasks.design: Vacancies start from a role profile template in the recruitment system ({ATS}) and, once the supervisor has finished the text, go to several job sites at once. Applications arrive in the same system with answers to short questions on availability and certificates; the supervisor reads every application and no rule or model rejects anyone. Candidates pick an interview slot from the supervisor's calendar ({CALENDAR}). After the supervisor decides, the offer goes out from a template. Interviewing and deciding stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vacancies were posted site by site and applications sat in an e-mail inbox.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitment systems post to many job sites and offer interview slot booking.
tasks.still_hard: Good service workers are scarce, so applications are few.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing in an interview whether someone enjoys looking after people.

evidence.claim: Recruitment systems post vacancies to several job sites and let candidates book interview slots.
AI used to filter applications or evaluate candidates is high-risk under Annex III point 4(a), so screening stays rule-free and human.

assumptions: Boundary: from the vacancy need to the offer sent; contracts and onboarding are outside.
Input contract: role profiles from HR; job site links set up by HR; fallback is posting by hand and e-mail.
Candidates answer two short questions and pick a slot instead of e-mailing back and forth; no added candidate time.
Interviewing and deciding do not change.
research_questions: Does time from vacancy to offer fall?

incremental.description: Service supervisor keeps interview slots open in the calendar.

approvals.approved_version: The vacancy text as finished by the supervisor in s1.
The hiring decision and offer terms as decided by the supervisor in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one hire a year; high: frequent hiring with many applications.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The service supervisor keeps training on the floor, meeting managers, judging rosters and hiring; explaining policies one by one, scattered memos, spreadsheet rosters and posting vacancies by hand shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who spends saved time coaching staff on the floor.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
